reason: Attacked and it held. Wording and lineation: sanmateobuddhisttemple.org/from-issas-the-year-of-my-life prints the verse as four lines, 'The world of dew / Is the world of dew, / And yet . . . / And yet . . .', with exactly these capitals and the spaced ellipses, inside the passage on the daughter's death, and cites The Year of My Life: A Translation of Issa's Oraga Haru, trans. Nobuyuki Yuasa, pages 103 to 104. No drift from the named translator. Locator: the verifier's correction is the right one. The dew verse is not the last poem of Oraga Haru; the work closes on the verse of trust in Amida at the year's end, and the note now says so plainly. One error is in the evidence rather than in anything that ships: the closing haiku is tomokaku mo anata makase no toshi no kure, not nanigoto mo; the note itself carries no transliteration, so nothing false reaches the card. Attribution: not in the misattribution list; the CFL line it replaces, 'This world of dew is a world of dew, and yet, and yet', is an unattributed floating rendering and the proposal has correctly gone back to a named translation. Checks: shipped [] and near [] for the lineated form, for a run-together form and for the CFL prose form; Issa at 2 for the year from months 2 and 4, so this is his third and last, at cap but not over. Scope, publishability: the verse itself carries no image of dying and needs no warning. Three things for the editor rather than refutations. First, the quotation ends on an ellipsis, so the last character is a full stop only by accident; it cannot be altered without minting, and the rule's purpose is met. Second, 'the elegy for his daughter' sits in the source line between locator and translation, which rule 5 reserves for a speaker, and it also puts a dead child in the byline at six in the morning when the note already carries the fact; the betterCitation drops it. Third, this line and 08-cfl-06 are both Nobuyuki Yuasa, and the Li Bai carry-in note records the practice that only one poem per translator stands in a month, so the editor must drop one or accept the doubling knowingly. Not refuted.
betterCitation: Kobayashi Issa, The Year of My Life, pp. 103 to 104 (trans. Nobuyuki Yuasa, 1960)
